---
title: "Getting started"
---

Build the release shell from a checkout of this repository. The `duckdb` submodule must be the pinned 2.0 alpha. Do not point these examples at a PyPI or CRAN DuckDB: those clients are 1.x and cannot load `duckboost`.

## Build

```bash
git submodule update --init --recursive
make
make test
```

`make` writes `./build/release/duckdb` (the CLI, with duckboost statically linked) and `./build/release/extension/duckboost/duckboost.duckdb_extension` (the loadable extension). `make test` runs the SQL tests under `test/sql/`.

`GEN=ninja make` uses Ninja when it is installed. The default target is the release build.

## Load an unsigned local build

Open the shell with `-unsigned` so DuckDB accepts an extension that was not signed for a release:

```bash
./build/release/duckdb -unsigned
```

```sql
LOAD 'build/release/extension/duckboost/duckboost.duckdb_extension';
```

The `make` shell also registers duckboost statically, so `LOAD duckboost;` works in that binary without the path. The path form is what you use when you load the `.duckdb_extension` file into a DuckDB 2.0 shell that was not built with this repository's `Makefile`.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from _helpers.duckrun import show

show("""
LOAD 'build/release/extension/duckboost/duckboost.duckdb_extension';
SELECT backend, training_supported, notes
FROM duckboost_backends()
ORDER BY backend;
""")
```

`training_supported` is true only for backends this binary can train in-process. A default `make` enables the native histogram trainer (`backend` column still reads `reference` in `duckboost_backends()` / model JSON; pass `backend = 'native'` in train options). XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost stay import-only unless you linked the vendor libraries.

## First model

Train a small body-mass regression on the [Palmer penguins](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/) CSV loaded from its public raw URL. Named features, an explicit target, and a holdout-style training RMSE show the usual tabular loop: table → feature list → `duckboost_train` → metric. Each block on this site starts a new in-memory database; released DuckDB autoloads `httpfs` for HTTPS `read_csv`.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from _helpers.duckrun import show

show("""
LOAD duckboost;

CREATE TABLE penguins AS
SELECT
  body_mass_g::DOUBLE AS body_mass_g,
  [bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm, flipper_length_mm, (sex = 'male')::DOUBLE] AS features
FROM read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/allisonhorst/palmerpenguins/master/inst/extdata/penguins.csv', nullstr = 'NA')
WHERE body_mass_g IS NOT NULL
  AND bill_length_mm IS NOT NULL
  AND sex IS NOT NULL;

CREATE TABLE models AS
SELECT duckboost_train(
  body_mass_g, features,
  MAP {
    'backend': 'native',
    'n_estimators': '40',
    'max_depth': '3',
    'learning_rate': '0.15',
    'feature_names': 'bill_length_mm,bill_depth_mm,flipper_length_mm,male'
  }
) AS model
FROM penguins;

SELECT round(duckboost_evaluate_agg(
  model, body_mass_g, features, MAP {'metric': 'rmse'}
), 1) AS rmse_g
FROM models, penguins;
""")
```

A few predictions next to the measured mass:

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from _helpers.duckrun import show

show("""
LOAD duckboost;

CREATE TABLE penguins AS
SELECT
  body_mass_g::DOUBLE AS body_mass_g,
  [bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm, flipper_length_mm, (sex = 'male')::DOUBLE] AS features
FROM read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/allisonhorst/palmerpenguins/master/inst/extdata/penguins.csv', nullstr = 'NA')
WHERE body_mass_g IS NOT NULL
  AND bill_length_mm IS NOT NULL
  AND sex IS NOT NULL;

CREATE TABLE models AS
SELECT duckboost_train(
  body_mass_g, features,
  MAP {
    'backend': 'native',
    'n_estimators': '40',
    'max_depth': '3',
    'learning_rate': '0.15',
    'feature_names': 'bill_length_mm,bill_depth_mm,flipper_length_mm,male'
  }
) AS model
FROM penguins;

SELECT
  round(body_mass_g, 0) AS body_mass_g,
  round(duckboost_predict(model, features), 0) AS pred_g
FROM models, penguins
ORDER BY body_mass_g
LIMIT 5;
""")
```
